column4: A bit flip in a temporary row cache now triggers a rebuild instead of silently changing recorded statistics.
Older row caches rebuild once from original run logs, then remain available for normal fast reloads.
Cache writing computes its integrity check directly from the existing buffer, preserving raw-history formats and avoiding another full-size copy.
Added tests for bit flips, valid-text damage, older cache migration and unchanged genuine history; existing allocation checks still exercise malformed payloads.
Recorded the preceding Sort fix's Android evidence, cache corruption reproductions and remaining audit limitations.
I added an integrity check to temporary row caches because valid-looking text could still be damaged. Original run logs stay untouched, and older caches rebuild safely.
